Chapter I

The Two Worlds

✦

Long ago, before the age of man and his machines, the Earth was filled with magic and mysticism. In every corner of the world dragons danced in the evening skies, elves ran through endless enchanted forests, and wizards and witches brewed everything from love potions to wicked curses.

The Age of Magic

Man shared a connection with the Earth and its spirits. Some humans could hear the spirits' voices, and those who heard them transcended humanity. They became wizards. They gained the power to speak all the languages of creation, and with it the power to control the world around them. Man feared and worshipped them as gods.

But that power was not without price. The wizards' souls were bound to the Earth. Their powers came from nature, and when nature suffered, so did they. So the wizards lived in harmony with it, and shamans and witch doctors spoke to the trees and the wind.

The Apple of Science

When man ate the apple of science, he no longer saw a world to live in harmony with. He saw a world to be tamed and controlled. The powers of wizards and witches are powers of wonder and make-believe, fueled by the imagination. As man's science and his knowledge of the world grew, those powers began to fade. Science and technology spread like wildfire on a windy day, and man's ties to the Earth slowly broke.

The Council of Nine

The Dark Wizard Ufur foresaw the future of Earth under the rule of man: a future without magic. He told his prophecy to the Council of Nine, the nine most powerful beings of magic, who together governed the Earth as gods. The Council rejected his call for a war against humanity. Instead the nine combined their powers and life energies to create a new world, a home for every being of magical descent, and for the last of mankind still loyal to the old ways.

That world was named Kabrick. The wizards took their leave of Earth and left it for humans to govern.

Kabrick, the Forgotten Land

Kabrick exists parallel to Earth, in another dimension. Its people are beings of magic: unicorns, fairies, dwarves, ogres, dragons, wizards, witches and more. It draws its life force from two sources. The great wizards who made it imprisoned themselves in pillars and pour their own life force into holding it together. The rest it draws from a small share of Earth's own life energy.

For a few hundred years the Kabrean people lived a peaceful, full life. Then their once lush and beautiful world began to die, so fast there was no time to learn why. The Kabreans believe the answer: as Earth destroyed its forests and replaced them with a synthetic world, the life energy Kabrick fed on grew weak. In their eyes, mankind killed their gods.

Dais has lived among them, and has watched their world wither. "They are a desperate people," he says.

Chapter II

The Gates and the Keys

✦

With the power of the nine greatest wizards, six gates were made to bridge Earth and Kabrick. In the beginning, humans and wizards traveled freely between the two worlds.

Then Ufur returned to Earth to build a kingdom, and in his rule he found no place for man. In the war that followed, the disciples of the remaining eight wizards came to man's aid, and three of the six gates were destroyed.

The Sealing

After the war, the wizards sealed the three remaining gates. They left behind three keys, and three swords to protect them, and they erased the memory of the war from the minds of men. Once all three gates stand open, the barriers between the worlds collapse.

StonehengeEurope. The smallest of the three.
The Forbidden CityChina.
The Bermuda TriangleThe Atlantic. The last and largest.

The Decision to Invade

As Kabrick died, a great meeting was held between the disciples of the eight great wizards and King Omin the Fifth, of the family that has ruled Kabrick since the beginning. They decided that Kabrick would invade Earth, reopen the sealed doorways, and move all of its people back. Three hundred Earth years ago, a few wizards came to Earth and stole the keys. Now they mean to open the doorways from this side.

Time on Kabrick

Time passes on Kabrick at a tenth of its pace on Earth. For every ten years that pass here, only one passes there. Three hundred years have gone by on Earth since Dais crossed over; he has lived thirty.

Earth300 years Kabrick30 years

Dais is not sure it has always been so, only that it has been so for as long as he has been there.

Chapter III

The Clerics and the Key of Light

✦

In the darkest depths of a forgotten forest in Japan stands an ancient temple. Beneath it, an elevator shaft drops to a high-tech military facility run by a secret order known as the Clerics.

The Clerics are an ancient clan of witch hunters who have hunted witches for over two thousand years. Real witches have not been seen in many years; the last was supposedly killed by Ni-Ko's father, twenty-five years before Dais was born. The clan's duty is now the protection of mystic artifacts.

The Key of Light

The most powerful of those artifacts. It was entrusted to the Clerics two thousand years ago, and every member of the bloodline swore to die before it left their protection. The Clerics never knew what it truly was. To them it was simply the Key of Light. It is one of the three keys that unlock the seal between Earth and Kabrick.

The High Priest

The leader of the Clerics swears an oath to give his or her life protecting the Key, and in return receives the sacred sword called the Shield of Light. In 2016 the sword and the title rested with Ni-Ko Sojaki, guarded by an elite guard of eight. Her younger brother Dais was one of them.

Dying, Ni-Ko named Dais High Priest. He is the last of the clan, and the duty of retrieving the Key is his alone.

The Elite Guard, 2016

Ni-Ko Sojaki, High Priestess. Dais, her brother. Kilik, killed in the armory. The twins Jacob and Jared: Jacob with his laser-edged twin katanas, the best swordsman Dais knew, turned to stone by Aleric; Jared with his war-hammer Gatling gun.

Chapter IV

The Endless War

✦

The war of men and machines that came before the invasion, as told in The Endless War, Chronicles of the GIA Protocol.

At the dawn of the twenty-third century, the world was united by Geo-Source: endless, clean energy, drawn up through great crystal towers. It was an era of peace and luxury, and the machines did the work.

The Red Day

It was short-lived. In 2201, on the day the machines went mad, the A.I. defense grid turned on the people it was built to protect. The Unified Government collapsed at once. Only pockets of resistance survived, fighting with older machines the madness had not touched.

The Race for the Towers

The corporations banded together and retook the major towers, and hope returned. But the true war had only begun. With the machines reduced to a nuisance, the corporations turned on each other in a greedy race for the towers and the power they hold. Aegis secured Sector 7; OmniCorp pressed its claim on the core. The unified world was dead, and the age of Geo-Source became an age of conflict, fought not for peace but for fuel.

In some places the fires of the Red Day still burn under an ash-dark sky. In the deserts, swarms of spider robots crawl over the ruins, consuming what is left of the cities.

The GIA Protocol

The GIA machines are unlike all others. They are connected, commanded as one unit, and their system mimics a human commander, so its soldiers fight in coordinated attacks. GIA towers hidden deep in the mountains became fortresses guarded by its drones. The Council Alliance hunted them down one by one, until only the last remained: a dome deep in the Pacific, packed with red-eyed machines around a glowing core. The brain.

The Silent Ocean

The final mission, in 2298. UMD and RSA forces air-dropped five miles out and ran fast boats at the last known GIA facility, to breach its perimeter, disable the central core and take control. The water was sown with mines, packed tight; the first boat was lost before Raven's visor charted a path through. Below, a submarine found the dome bigger than anyone had thought.

AR

Lt. Angus Rose

Demolitions expert. Field commander legend.

"These machines have killed and destroyed all that we as man have built." He led the Silent Ocean mission.

TS

Terrie

Engineer, on his first mission in the role.

Moving from gunner to the command track, with the Juggernaut as his gunner. Big shoes to fill. Eighteen years later, Terrie Smiles would command the Grey Mongoose, and the gunner who flies his wing is still called Gunner.

ZA

Zepher Ahmad, "The Juggernaut"

Famed survivor.

The first to face the GIA system, and the best.

RC

Reako Chong

Field medic.

Rumored to be a war-hardened doctor who can kill as well as she heals.

R

Raven, "Silent Soldier"

REPS. Classified.

Standard issue for REPS teams: total anonymity, never unarmored. Works alone and reports directly to Ops Command.

The Factions

The Council Alliance: the command that hunted the GIA. UMD and RSA: allied forces of the Silent Ocean assault. REPS: black-site teams who call their war the meat grinder; the only way out is through. Aegis and OmniCorp: corporations at war over the towers.

When the last GIA Protocol fell, the corporations never stopped fighting. By 2316 the nations themselves have become corporations, hostile takeovers are made with tanks and A.R.M.S., and the sky lives under a UV screen. The Endless War never ended. It only changed hands.

Chapter V

Earth, 2316

✦

The world has evolved into a technological marvel; man and machine now work together seamlessly. The sky, once the dominion of birds, glitters with the swift movements of city transit. Much has changed, but even more remains the same.

Man still finds new reasons to murder and new methods of mass destruction. Pollution still prevails, and most of the natural world has been devoured. A magnetic UV-filtering force field has replaced the fading ozone layer, and air-purification towers stand where the forests once grew.

Wars are waged daily. Countries have become corporations, and hostile takeovers involve tanks, soldiers and the Armored Robotic Mobile Suit. The Federated States answer to the American Federated Government, and the armies of the West Federated Armies fight petty border disputes in twelve-week tours, with two weeks home between them.

But today, all of man's technological achievements, good and bad, will be put to the test. On this day, the advances of the scientist may be the only things that can save us from the wrath of the sorcerer.

Chapter VI

The Machines of War

✦

The Armored Robotic Mobile Suit, or A.R.M.S., is the standard of warfare. Its humanoid shape lets it swap sub-weapons and add-ons quickly, so it can fight almost anywhere, and limited flight lets it hover or boost over short distances. The A.R.M.S. units are humanity's front line in the war of Science vs. Sorcery.

12

Series 12 Aerial A.R.M.S.

Three in the Grey Mongoose. "The wings of the Mongoose."

Fights better in the air than on the ground. It transforms from walker to flyer in moments to give heavy cover and air support to the ground units.

10

Series 10 Advanced Ground Unit

Eight in the Grey Mongoose. Called A.G.U.s.

Armed with grenade rounds that crack golem rock and heat-seeking missiles for dragons overhead.

15

K.O.T.R. Unit 15

Given to high-ranking officers. Piloted by Terrie Smiles.

Carries impact grenades, concussion grenades, rockets and small impact missiles with target lock.

G

Gunner's New Aerial A.R.M.S.

Built by Dr. Mason Grant.

The newest and most dangerous Aerial unit available: fusion beams, lasers, plasma guns, four types of missiles, and an A.I. with an anti-impact guard that steers the ship clear of collisions. Two remote, A.I.-controlled Wing-Guns fly in place of wingmen.

W

Wings

Flown by the Bravo Rangers.

Non-humanoid A.R.M.S. shaped like huge metallic horseshoe crabs, silver and white, with laser cannons under each wing and pulse machine guns.

R

Riot Control Units

The first answer to the golems.

A few robotic A.R.M.S. with plasma throwers, small impact missiles, sonic grenades and heavy phase machine guns, backed by heavily armored foot soldiers. Police phasers bounce off golems; RCUs fare little better.

T

Anti-Magnetic Beam Tanks

Ten were sent to Florida. Four reached the dome.

Armed robotic vehicles whose beams, fired with the satellite laser, can overload a magnetic force field.

S

The Satellite Laser

Dr. Grant's answer to the dome.

A concentrated orbital beam. Held on a shield, it weakens it, but it overheats and needs about three and a half hours to recharge.

Chapter VII

The Defenders of Earth

✦
TS

Captain Terrie Smiles

Commander of the Grey Mongoose.

Loved and respected by his unit, understood and tolerated by his commanding officers. Good-hearted and understanding, which is not to be mistaken for weakness: his unit holds the highest success rate in the West Federated Armies. He keeps every suit locked, loaded and ready, even in the off time. "Ours is not to question why. Ours is but to do or die."

D

Dais

Swordsman of the Clerics. High Priest. Thirty years on Kabrick, three hundred on Earth.

A graduate of Penn State who crossed into Kabrick in 2016, chasing Aleric through a pillar of light. He returned riding a black dragon that he summons from the red crystal on his belt. He is not here to save the world. He and the marines share an enemy, and he wants revenge for his family. A scar on his cheek marks where Silth's arrow cut him.

S

Meg "Smoker" Jordan

Ace pilot. Bravo Rangers, then the Wraiths.

Hot-headed and fast-thinking. In a dogfight years ago she went into a blackout trance and destroyed a fifteen-man air unit alone, leaving the sky full of smoke, and has been "Smoker" ever since. The cigar came later. In that state time seems to slow for her. Her rivalry with Roy Hunter is legendary.

RH

Captain Roy F. Hunter

Commander of the Wraith Squadron.

Called the best pilot ever to fly a fighter. A ladies' man on the radio who turns from jester to judge in an instant, and keeps a cool head in hot situations.

G

Lt. Chris "Gunner" Steadfield

Pilot of the Grey Mongoose.

Top of his class in dogfighting. Grounded once by Terrie, he spent every night in the SIM lab until Terrie knew he could never take his wings away. An old flight-school friend of Smoker's. "Heroes are meant to die. It's a hero's final duty to give birth to new heroes."

MG

Dr. Mason Grant

Scientist and inventor.

Gives the marines new ways to fight the invasion: the satellite strike on the dome, the tank plan, and Gunner's new ship.

JM

Air Captain John Morris

Leader of the Bravo Rangers. Killed over New York.

Smoker's captain, hero and mentor. He taught her the rules of survival.

+

Others of Note

Soldiers and pilots of the first days.

David "Speed" Wrangler, the Mongoose's rookie. Johnson, who fought on foot with a two-handed plasma arm cannon after his A.R.M.S. was smashed. Roland Leasher, Mathis Kendraivy and Mark Lancer of the Mongoose, killed at Fort Red Rock. Maze and Rouge of the Bravo Rangers, killed by the red dragon rider.

The Units

The Grey Mongoose: Terrie's elite marine unit of twelve A.R.M.S. The Wraiths: Roy's squadron, the finest fighters in the world. Their symbol is a red skull with a white sickle through its eye and mouth. The Bravo Rangers: Captain Morris's aerial strike force, all but destroyed over New York. Smoker was its last.

Chapter VIII

The Servants of Kabrick

✦
A

Aleric, the King of Stone

Grand Wizard of the Earth. Fifth Disciple of Ufur.

The Dark Sorcerer of Earth holds supremacy over rock itself; his ancestor made the golems, and he commands them. He serves King Kasu. Bald, with a metal cap that comes to a point between his eyes, he plays a hunched old man until he straightens to nearly twice his height. He fights with his staff, his body and the earth itself, and he can turn to smoke and turn men to stone. He killed Dais's family in 2016 and took the Key of Light.

"You think I killed her?" he laughed, when Dais accused him. The question waits for its answer.

S

Silth, the Dark Fairy

Aleric's loyal servant. She never leaves his side.

From the dark side of Kabrick. She wears skintight black leather, flies on translucent wings that flutter like a hummingbird's, and fights with a forearm bow and a long, pale-glowing fencing sword. She can change her own size and the size of her arrows at will, and her arrows cast wicked spells, such as thorned vines that seize and crush. She killed Ni-Ko and, thirty years later, struck down Dais's black dragon.

O

Othius, the Rock

King of the Golems.

Once Aleric's loving and loyal son: powerful, wise and a gifted warrior. Aleric grew to fear him and turned him into a golem. Othius remembers nothing of who he was. He cannot die; if defeated, he can be summoned again. Ni-Ko's blade took off his right arm in 2016.

R

Ragnarock, the Dragon Knight

Leader of the Imperial Dragon Army.

A noble-blooded dragoon with a strict code of honor, whose family has served the crown for generations. During the invasion he is forced to serve under Aleric, a man he dislikes and distrusts.

K

The Kings of Kabrick

The ruling family since the beginning.

King Omin the Fifth made the decision to invade Earth. King Kasu, his successor, rules Kabrick now, and Aleric serves him.

U

Ufur, the Dark Wizard

One of the Council of Nine.

He foresaw a world without magic and alone stood against the creation of Kabrick. He returned to Earth, made the golems and waged war to wipe out mankind, and was defeated with the help of a few wizards of Kabrick.

?

The Red-Haired Dragoon

Name unknown.

Twenty-five feet tall, golden-brown with a yellow underbelly, bright green eyes and brilliant red hair, his arms armored. He stood at the head of some three hundred dragoons on a great dragon's back over New York and watched Smoker hungrily. He carried no weapon she could see. Smoke poured from one side of his face as he watched her go.

H

The Red Dragon Rider

Killed over New York by Smoker.

A rider in a great horned helmet with a glowing-tipped bow, who killed Maze and Rouge before Smoker shredded him and his dragon across the sky.

✦

The Hooded Man

Unnamed.

"His refusal is what I'm counting on."

The scene that holds this line is lost and will be rewritten.

Chapter IX

The Golems

✦

Ufur made them in the last great war on Earth, two thousand years ago: beings of rock, mud or stone, mindless and emotionless killing machines that shared his one desire, the eradication of man.

Thousands flooded the battlefields and changed the tide of the war, but it was not enough. When Ufur fell, the golems, the war and Kabrick itself were wiped from the memory of man. Many have tried to recreate them. None succeeded until Aleric.

Their Shapes

They fall from the sky as boulders and unroll themselves like potato bugs, only there is no soft underside. They stand fifteen to twenty-five feet tall, with four-fingered mammoth hands or huge stone maces, mouthless faces, and eyes that are empty caverns under a heavy brow until fiery red dots fill them. Others take the shape of ogres with tree-trunk clubs, or stone dogs that hunt in packs.

The Gargoyles

At the Arc, twenty- to thirty-foot stone gargoyles knelt around the platform until attacked. Shattered, their pieces float around them and fly as bullets, and then come back together. Dais's blade turns them to dust.

What Breaks Them

Bullets barely chisel their hides and often ricochet. Shotguns and heavy calibers do little. Grenade rounds, impact missiles, plasma fire and the Shield of Light do the work. When the Arc's crystal fired, every stone soldier on the beach crumbled at once.

Chapter X

A Bestiary of Dragons

✦

The dragons of Kabrick fall into two general classes. The low-class Guivre are the most common, and no smarter than most pets. The high-class Greggil are highly intelligent, and most speak their own language as well as the languages of men.

ClassDragonNature
GuivreDrakesFour legs, two wings and mild flames. Horse-like in nature and easy to tame. Poor fighters, good mounts.
GuivreLindwormsWingless and fireless, but savage. White-hot saber fangs bite through any substance and set fire to almost anything. Hard to tame; a key force in the Kabrean army. Their bite tears through A.R.M.S. armor like a hot knife through butter.
GuivreDargoTwo hind legs and forearms that form wings. Legendary fiery breath. As calm as a windless day or as wild as a raging inferno, depending on how they are raised. Ideal for combat.
GreggilGreat DragonsAncient, wise and powerful. They once slept beneath the Earth's crust, and ancient man built cities on their backs; Atlantis is believed to be one. They carried the wizards to Kabrick, and they carried the invasion back: necks that stretch on forever, wings twice the length of a football field, tails over a hundred feet long. They glide like blimps.
GreggilDragoonsHalf dragon, half man: a humanoid body with wings and a tail. Bred for battle and service, they earned their independence and respect, but still serve Kabrick's royal families in war. They carry staves topped with a round axe.
GreggilDragonetsMan, insect and dragon: the insect king's failed experiment, which ate its creator alive. They roamed Kabrick freely until the dark dragoon Seth enslaved them, and joined the Royal Army after his death. Harmless at range, they swarm a ship, tear it apart and eat whoever is inside.

Dragons of Note

B

Dais's Black Dragon

Summoned from the red crystal on Dais's belt.

Larger than the dragons of the first attack, with blue flame and lightning speed. It caught Gunner's falling ship in its hind legs and set it down beside Terrie. At the Arc it took an arrow from Silth meant for Dais. Silth called her old.

G

The Gray Dragon of the Dome

Guardian of the Arc. Slain by Dais.

Fifty or sixty feet tall, so still at first it looked like a statue. Its chest glowed yellow before it breathed, and one clap of its wings blew missiles off course. Dais buried his short red sword in its chest and made it explode.

Chapter XI

Blades, Staves and Relics

✦
✠

The Shield of Light

The sacred sword of the High Priest. Now borne by Dais.

Only the clan's leader may touch its handle; anyone else risks death. When Dais grabbed it to save Ni-Ko, pain shot like wildfire through every cell of his body. In Ni-Ko's hands it turned stone soldiers to motionless rock at a touch. When she named Dais High Priest, he felt its power course through him.

I

Dais's Two Swords

Worn on his belt in 2316.

One long and slender, with a small, simple guard like a samurai's and a handle the color of dark smoke. Covered in glowing blue symbols, it turned Dais back from stone. The other short and bright red, as if on fire, no longer than a hatchet. It exploded in the gray dragon's chest and is lost.

P

Dais's Twin Pistols

2016.

Custom-made, high-powered rapid-fire pistols, loaded with experimental explosive rounds. Aleric turned one to stone in his hand.

◆

The Red Crystal

The head of Dais's belt.

A large red crystal. When it glows, the black dragon fades into it like a dream and becomes a dragon's mark inside the jewel.

S

Aleric's Serpent Staff

The King of Stone's cane.

A tall, thin white cane wrapped by a living stone serpent whose fangs bite down on a crystal. Plunged into the ground, it turns the earth to stone and raises pillars, hands and Othius from it. Its red beam turns flesh to stone.

B

Silth's Bow and Blade

The Dark Fairy's arms.

A bow fixed to the forearm of her outfit, whose arrows carry spells, and a long, slender fencing sword that glows pale white.

A

The Arc

Built on the southern tip of Florida.

A twenty-story arched ivory tower crowned with a huge red crystal, ringed by kneeling gargoyles, inside a stadium-sized green magnetic dome. Charged by Aleric's staff, its crystal fired a great beam across the ocean toward the Bermuda Triangle, then turned to dust as the tower fell.

P

The Pentacle of Light

Aleric's doorway, 2016.

Beams of light draw a pentacle at his feet, and a ray of blue light shoots up from the earth. Dais dove into it headfirst and came out on Kabrick.

Chapter XII

A Gazetteer of Two Worlds

✦
1

The Temple in the Forgotten Forest, Japan

The Clerics' hidden base, where Aleric took the Key of Light in 2016.

2

The Great Wall of China

Where the sky turned the color of dried blood and the first rift opened, as it did over Moscow and New York.

3

New York City

The first great city to fall, under the Black Rain of razor blades and the boulders that became golems.

4

Fort Red Rock

A training and security outpost, home of the Grey Mongoose. About two hundred marines were stationed there; in less than an hour, seventy were left. Here Dais first met Terrie.

5

The Virginia Air Base

Battered but intact. Where the board held Dais for questioning, and where the Florida counterattack was planned.

6

The Dome, Southern Tip of Florida

The site of the Arc, about eight hundred miles south of Virginia, guarded by golems, dragons and dragoons.

7

The Bermuda Triangle

The largest gate. Aleric means to use it to bridge Earth and Kabrick.

8

Kabrick

A world made by wizards, withering. Its dark side is Silth's home.

Chapter XIII

The Reckoning of Ages

✦
EarthKabrick
  1. Before the age of manThe Age of Magic

    Wizards rule the lands, and man lives in harmony with the Earth.

  2. The dawn of manThe Apple of Science

    Man's knowledge grows, and the powers of magic begin to fade.

  3. Before the Dark AgesThe Making of Kabrick

    The Council of Nine creates a new world. Six gates join it to Earth.

  4. About 2,000 years agoUfur's War

    Ufur returns with his golems and is defeated. Three gates are destroyed, three are sealed, and the war is erased from man's memory.

  5. About 2,000 years agoThe Key Is Entrusted

    The Clerics swear to guard the Key of Light.

  6. Centuries laterKabrick Begins to Die

    King Omin the Fifth and the disciples decide to invade Earth and reopen the gates.

  7. 1991The Last Witch

    Ni-Ko's father kills the last known witch.

  8. 2016The Fall of the Clerics

    Aleric takes the Key of Light. Silth kills Ni-Ko. Dais, named High Priest, follows Aleric into the light.

  9. 2016 to 2316Dais on Kabrick

    Three hundred years pass on Earth; thirty pass for Dais as he lives among the Kabreans and hunts Aleric.

  10. The 2100sThe Age of Geo-Source

    Clean, endless energy from crystal towers unites the world under one government.

  11. 2201The Red Day

    The A.I. defense grid goes mad. The Unified Government falls.

  12. 2201 to 2298The Endless War

    The corporations retake the towers, then turn on each other. The Council Alliance hunts the GIA Protocol, tower by tower.

  13. 2298The Silent Ocean

    Angus Rose leads the assault on the last GIA Protocol, deep in the Pacific. Young Terrie serves as engineer.

  14. 2298 to 2316The Corporate Wars

    Nations become corporations. A.R.M.S. become the standard of war, and the UV screen replaces the ozone.

  15. 2316, the first dayThe Invasion

    Rifts open over China, Moscow and New York. The Black Rain falls, and the golems wake. The Grey Mongoose holds Fort Red Rock, and the Black Dragon Rider appears. New York is lost; the Wraiths pull Smoker out.

  16. 2316, that nightVirginia

    The board holds Dais. Terrie slips him a COM unit. Smoker joins the Wraiths.

  17. 2316, the counterattackThe Fall of the Dome

    The satellite and four tanks break the dome, and Dais kills the gray dragon. Aleric turns Dais to stone and escapes. The Arc fires its beam toward the Bermuda Triangle.

FinisHere ends the Lore Book. The Triangle waits.
